headline: Softer volumes widen GAAP loss as capital funds M&A spree
summary_short: QXO's Q1 2026 net sales fell 21.1% q/q to $1,730.2M on softer building-products demand, with a GAAP net loss of $227.1M (-$0.35/share) and Adjusted EBITDA of just $1.2M, while cash rose to $3,046.3M after a $749M equity raise ahead of the Kodiak and TopBuild acquisitions.
summary_long: Q1 2026 net sales fell 21.1% q/q to $1,730.2M on building-products softness. Operating loss widened to $251.9M (from -$69.5M q/q), driven by restructuring ($16.3M), transaction ($19.3M) and transformation ($11.4M) costs atop Beacon integration investment. GAAP net loss was $227.1M (-$0.35/share); Adjusted Net Loss was $57.2M and Adjusted Diluted EPS -$0.12. Adjusted EBITDA was $1.2M, up from -$9.0M a year ago (pre-Beacon). Cash rose to $3,046.3M after a $749M equity raise and Series C Preferred commitments, funding the April 1 $2.25B Kodiak close and pending $17B TopBuild deal (Q3 close expected). No numeric guidance issued; management reaffirmed its long-term $50B revenue target.

drivers.explanation: Management cited softness in building-products industry demand this quarter, alongside continued investments in people and technology across the legacy Beacon business.
Widened q/q on $16.3M restructuring, $19.3M transaction and $11.4M transformation costs layered onto ongoing Beacon integration investment.
Not explained in the release; the y/y swing from -$9.0M coincides with net sales scaling from $13.5M to $1,730.2M after the Beacon Roofing acquisition closed in 2025.
Widened on the same operating-cost items plus a swing from $56.6M net interest income to $31.1M net interest expense, consistent with debt taken on for the Beacon acquisition.
Rose on $749.5M net proceeds from a January 2026 common stock offering and other financing inflows, partly offset by a $22.5M capex outflow.

Softer building-products demand hit a newly-consolidated Beacon business while capital raised (equity, Series C preferred) funded the April 1 $2.25B Kodiak close and the pending $17B TopBuild deal; no numeric forward guidance was issued.
